{"concepts_used":["GC-0115","GC-0131","GC-0091","GC-0092"],"decline_reason":"","declined":false,"citations":[{"ref":"TMM/Part2/4/part-2-4-3-fee-not-paid-or-underpaid","quote":"Where the Registrar fails to notify the person of an underpayment within 14 working days of the person making an application, notice or request, then the application, notice or request is treated as filed despite the failure to pay the relevant fee (reg 21.21A(2))."},{"ref":"TMM/Part4/6/6/3/3","quote":"If the Registrar does not notify the person within the 14 days allowed by subsection 223(5) (reg 21.23), the document is taken to be filed on the date it is received."},{"ref":"TMM/Part2/4/part-2-4-3-fee-not-paid-or-underpaid","quote":"However, reg 21.21A(2) does not have the effect of waiving the fee. The fee or amount unpaid remains a debt owed to the Commonwealth."},{"ref":"TMM/Part2/4/part-2-4-3-fee-not-paid-or-underpaid","quote":"If a fee is payable in respect of the doing of an act by the Registrar (such as the examination of a trade mark), the Registrar must not do that act until the fee has been paid (reg 21.21A(1))."},{"ref":"TMM/Part4/1/1/3/1","quote":"If the Registrar does not notify an applicant within 14 days of the underpayment or non-payment of the fee,the request is taken to be made, but the applicant must still be notified in writing of the deficiency in the fee as soon as practicable."}],"answer":"Under the supplied Manual practice:

• The application, notice or request is treated as filed if the Registrar fails to notify the person of the underpayment within 14 working days of making it (TMM/Part2/4/part-2-4-3-fee-not-paid-or-underpaid). The document-filing passage says the filing date is the date the document was received (TMM/Part4/6/6/3/3).
• The fee is not waived: the unpaid amount remains a debt owed to the Commonwealth (TMM/Part2/4/part-2-4-3-fee-not-paid-or-underpaid).
• Filing does not mean the Registrar can perform an act for which the fee is payable. For example, the Manual says examination must not occur until the relevant fee is paid (TMM/Part2/4/part-2-4-3-fee-not-paid-or-underpaid).
• The Manual also says written notification of the deficiency must still be given as soon as practicable (TMM/Part4/1/1/3/1).

These are statements of Manual practice, not independently verified statements of legislation. The supplied Act passages do not contain the fee provisions, and no Regulations passages are supplied. There is also a wording difference: Part 2 specifies ‘14 working days’, whereas the cited Part 4 passages say ‘14 days’. I cannot resolve that difference from the supplied legislation."}
